⚠️ Closed alpha — provisional docs. OpenDefence on Kubernetes (opendefence-platform) is in closed alpha and under rapid, breaking development. This page describes a moving target and will most likely be superseded by the documentation that ships with the first public release — treat everything here as provisional, and do not rely on it for a production deployment.

Every product on the platform — TAK, MediaMTX, Matrix, Battlelog — follows the same spoke pattern around the core services hub. This page describes that generic shape once, uses Battlelog as the minimal worked example, and stops there: per-product pod anatomies and port fleets live in the product books, and the step-by-step authoring workflow lives in the Build an integration book.

The spoke shape

A product integration is a self-contained Kustomize component under k8s/app-<short>/{base,overlays/{local,cloud}} that deploys into its own namespace app-<short> (app-tak, app-mtx, app-matrix, app-battlelog), applied in the final opendefence-apps phase after the core is up (see Deployment model). Inside that namespace the shape is always the same set of resources — the following diagram shows the full-featured version.

The standard parts, with the MediaMTX spoke as the concrete reference:

Part MediaMTX example Role
Namespace app-mtx Isolation boundary; everything the product owns lives here
Deployment (one pod, Recreate) mtx-server: mediamtx + mtx-ui-nginx + mtxrmapi The product itself plus its integration API in one pod
Integration API container mtxrmapi (ghcr.io/pvarki/mediamtx-integration:1.6.2-260707, port 8005) The contract surface rmapi talks to; must serve GET /api/v1/healthcheck
kraftwerk-init.json ConfigMap kraftwerk-init mounted at /pvarki Bootstrap file: where rasenmaeher is and which identity to trust (below)
CA trust mount ca-bundle ConfigMap key ca-cert.pem mounted at /ca_public Platform CA chain from the trust-manager Bundle (see PKI & trust)
Certificates mtx → secret mtx-tls (server); TAK adds a client cert tak-server-admin Issued by ClusterIssuer intermediate-ca-issuer; server cert backs the edge route, client certs where the product itself needs one
IngressRoute + TLSOption mtx on mtx.<domain>, mtls-strict, middleware mtls-chain-with-legacy Edge exposure through Traefik with edge-mTLS enforcement (see Ingress & network edge)
CNPG Cluster mtx-postgres → operator-generated secret mtx-postgres-app Dedicated database per product; credentials consumed from the generated Secret (see Data & secrets)
ExternalSecret mtx-secrets from Password generators Runtime passwords generated in-cluster by External Secrets Operator — nothing hand-provisioned
PVC mtx-data (1Gi) at /data/persistent Persistent product state
ServiceAccount + mesh SA mtx, pod annotation linkerd.io/inject: enabled Gives the pod the Linkerd identity mtx.app-mtx.serviceaccount.identity.linkerd.cluster.local (see Service mesh)

The bootstrap file is the piece that makes the pod platform-aware. Each product mounts its own kraftwerk-init.json at /pvarki, telling the integration API where rasenmaeher is and — critically — which mesh identity to accept. This is MediaMTX's local-overlay file verbatim:

{
  "deployment": "localmaeher",
  "rasenmaeher": {
    "init": {
      "base_uri": "https://localmaeher.dev.pvarki.fi/"
    },
    "mtls": {
      "base_uri": "http://rmapi.opendefence-system.svc.cluster.local:8000/"
    },
    "certcn": "rmapi.opendefence-system.serviceaccount.identity.linkerd.cluster.local"
  },
  "product": {
    "dns": "mtx.localmaeher.dev.pvarki.fi",
    "api": "https://mtx.localmaeher.dev.pvarki.fi/",
    "uri": "https://mtx.localmaeher.dev.pvarki.fi:9996/"
  }
}

rasenmaeher.mtls.base_uri is plain in-cluster HTTP — the mesh wraps it in mTLS transparently — and certcn pins the exact Linkerd identity the caller must present. With env MTLS_TRUST_L5D=true (MediaMTX also sets RMMTX_RMCN to the same value), the integration API rejects any in-mesh caller that is not rmapi. Several product pods (MediaMTX, Matrix — like rmapi itself) additionally mount a container-init.sh startup script that loads the CA bundle into the container's OS trust store — a self-described hack. Each app generates its own copy as a ConfigMap (container-init-hack in app-mtx, matrix-container-init in app-matrix); only the core reuses the shared k8s/_shared/rmapi-container-init component.

Registration and discovery

Discovery is deliberately dumb: a static registry, no service catalog. The hub side mirrors the spoke side — rmapi mounts the ConfigMap kraftwerk-rasenmaeher-init at its own /pvarki, mapping each product short name to its in-cluster Service URL and expected mesh identity:

{
  "dns": "localmaeher.dev.pvarki.fi",
  "deployment": "localmaeher",
  "products": {
    "tak": {
      "api": "http://tak-server.app-tak.svc.cluster.local:8003/",
      "uri": "https://tak.localmaeher.dev.pvarki.fi:8443/",
      "certcn": "tak.app-tak.serviceaccount.identity.linkerd.cluster.local"
    },
    "mtx": {
      "api": "http://mtx-server-internal.app-mtx.svc.cluster.local:8005/",
      "uri": "https://mtx.localmaeher.dev.pvarki.fi:9996/",
      "certcn": "mtx.app-mtx.serviceaccount.identity.linkerd.cluster.local"
    },
    "matrix": {
      "api": "http://matrix.app-matrix.svc.cluster.local:8012/",
      "uri": "https://matrix.localmaeher.dev.pvarki.fi:9996/",
      "certcn": "matrix.app-matrix.serviceaccount.identity.linkerd.cluster.local"
    }
  }
}

Note there are two distinct trust mechanisms, one per traffic direction:

  • User traffic arrives from outside through Traefik. The client certificate is verified at the edge against the ca-bundle, and the callsign middleware chain stamps Callsign / Callsign-Valid headers after checking validity with rmapi. Products trust those headers because the default strip-identity-headers middleware guarantees a client can never inject them.
  • Hub traffic (rmapi ↔ integration API) never leaves the cluster. Both ends are meshed, Linkerd provides workload mTLS, and each side pins the other's certcn from its /pvarki file — the product accepts only rmapi's identity, and rmapi expects the identity listed in its registry entry.

First contact between hub and spoke follows from those two files, shown here as a sequence.

The integration API's /api/v1/healthcheck doubles as the pod's own probe (the readiness comment in mtx-server.deployment.yaml is explicit: don't send traffic until the certs directory is populated), so "healthy to Kubernetes" and "healthy to rasenmaeher" are the same signal.

Battlelog: the minimal worked example

Battlelog (k8s/app-battlelog/) is the floor of the pattern — the smallest thing that still counts as an integration. One container, battlelog (ghcr.io/pvarki/blapi:1.0.0-d2.5.0, port 3000), serves both the product and its integration API; its health endpoint sits under the integration prefix at /rmapi/api/v1/healthcheck. The whole user path is a straight line.

blocks.html:
What it has: the namespace app-battlelog; the Deployment and Service; a Certificate battlelog from intermediate-ca-issuer backing secret battlelog-tls; an IngressRoute on bl.<domain> with TLSOption mtls-strict (a valid client certificate is required, not optional) plus the mtls-chain middleware; CNPG cluster battlelog-postgres on the PostGIS image (ghcr.io/cloudnative-pg/postgis:18-3.6-system-trixie) with a CNPG Database CR enabling the postgis, postgis_topology, fuzzystrmatch and postgis_tiger_geocoder extensions; and the battlelog-data PVC (5Gi) at /data/persistent. Database credentials come solely from the operator-generated battlelog-postgres-app Secret.

What it deliberately omits: the pod is not Linkerd-injected, there is no ExternalSecret, no /pvarki bootstrap file, no /ca_public mount — and consequently no entry in rmapi's product registry, so the hub never calls it. Being unmeshed means Battlelog cannot verify a caller's Linkerd identity at all; its only notion of "who is this user" is the edge-verified callsign headers Traefik forwards after the strict-mTLS handshake and validity check. That trade-off is acceptable exactly because the route is mtls-strict: nothing reaches blapi without a valid platform client certificate.

Where the pattern gets heavier

Everything above Battlelog is the same shape with more containers in the Deployment. TAK runs a ten-container pod (three init containers plus five JVM services split from one TAK image, an nginx, and the takrmapi integration API) — see the TAK stack page. MediaMTX adds a fleet of raw TCP/UDP media ports that bypass Traefik entirely — see MediaMTX stack. Matrix is the heaviest: six containers including Synapse, the Matrix Authentication Service and LiveKit, with its own OIDC registration against Keycloak at first boot — see Matrix stack. All three still boil down to the first diagram on this page; the product books document only what each adds on top.

Building your own integration

If you want to write an integration rather than understand the shape, that is a separate book: start with the integration overview, then set up your dev environment (Kubernetes) and register your integration (Kubernetes) — the last one walks through exactly the registry entry and kraftwerk-init.json wiring described above. One warning from the platform repo's own guidance: copy the per-service layout the products use, not k8s/opendefence-system — the core's aggregate base is flagged as a legacy anti-pattern.
